title: The Best Drift Alternatives in 2026: A Buyer's Guide to Replacing Drift Without Losing Pipeline
summary: Drift is being sunset. Compare 9 Drift alternatives and Drift chatbot replacements by pricing, CRM fit and pipeline impact. Picks from Storylane's CMO.
body_markdown:
*Last updated: October 2026. Pricing and product facts below were re-checked against each vendor's own site this month.*


Drift is being sunset, so if you are reading this you are shopping for a Drift alternative on a deadline. I'm Madhav, CMO at Storylane, and my advice before you shortlist any of the Drift alternatives below is to name the real problem first. It is not that your chatbot looks dated. It is the dark funnel.[Our research found that 2 in 3 buyer questions arrive when your sales team isn't around](https://www.storylane.io/blog/sales-agents-vs-human-reps-buyer-conversations) , which means the first answer a buyer gets comes from your website, not your rep. Most sites meet that moment with a form fill or a "someone will be in touch" bot. The answer existed; the channel to deliver it did not.


So I am not going to rank these tools on chat polish. I rank them on one question: do they actually answer buyers while they evaluate, and can you measure whether they got answered. That is answer rate, and in my experience it predicts pipeline better than any chat metric.[Conversational marketing](https://www.storylane.io/blog/conversational-marketing-strategy) is the broader category; what follows is my shortlist of what actually replaces Drift without rebuilding the same blind spot, plus the cutover plan I would run.


## Drift alternatives at a glance (comparison table)


Here is the short version, matched to primary need and grounded in each vendor's published pricing as of October 2026. Treat it as a scorecard, not a beauty contest. I put RepX first because it is our product and it is built for the core inbound job, and I list each competitor for the specialty it genuinely owns, including where it falls short.


Tool Best for Standout capability Pricing model (published) Where it falls short


**Storylane RepX** Demo-led inbound qualification on your own content AI agent trained on your docs, site, decks and interactive demos; shows the demo inside the conversation From $2,000/mo (Growth, up to 20,000 monthly visitors); Premium from $3,000/mo; 30-day free trial Inbound only, no outbound prospecting; video avatar and de-anonymization sit on Premium


**Qualified (Piper)** Salesforce-centric enterprise inbound Piper AI SDR across website chat, voice, video and email Quote-based (Premier, Enterprise, Ultimate); prices not public Built around Salesforce; now owned by Salesforce


**Spara** Inbound AI SDR across chat, email and voice Multi-channel agent; AI demos and de-anonymization on Growth Starter $2,100/mo, Growth $3,750/mo (billed annually) Voice, AI demos and de-anonymization are Growth-tier only


**Docket** Demand gen teams converting campaign traffic Agent grounded in a Sales Knowledge Lake, with multi-visit memory Growth $3,000/mo, Scale $4,000/mo (billed annually) Video avatar and multiple agents start on Scale


**Warmly** Visitor de-anonymization plus chat Person-level visitor identification with an Inbound Agent From $10,000/yr (de-anonymization); Inbound Chat $20,000/yr; AI Inbound Autopilot $30,000/yr Identification-first; AI chat is a higher tier


**1mind** Video-first AI avatar; Salesloft's referred successor Photorealistic "Superhumans" on the website, in product and on live calls Pricing not public; quote-based Enterprise sales motion; verify follow-up and identification coverage for your stack


**Intercom Fin** Support-led chat with some sales overlap Fin AI Agent, outcome-based pricing From $29/seat/mo (Essential, annual) plus $0.99 per Fin outcome Support-first; per-outcome cost scales with chat volume


**Knock AI** Messaging-app-first teams (Slack, LinkedIn, WhatsApp) AI SDR that meets buyers in the apps they already use Pipeline Foundation from $1,000 to $2,000/mo; Acceleration from $1,500 to $3,500/mo Multi-channel messaging needs the Acceleration tier


**Tidio** Budget and small teams Free live chat plus Lyro AI add-on Free; Starter $24.17/mo; Growth from $49.17/mo No account-based targeting for a B2B ABM motion


Pricing sources:[storylane.io/plans](https://www.storylane.io/plans) , qualified.com/pricing, spara.com/pricing,[docket.io/pricing](https://www.docket.io/pricing) , warmly.ai/pricing, intercom.com/pricing, knock-ai.com/pricing and tidio.com/pricing, all checked in October 2026. Verify before you buy; vendors change packaging often.


## Why Drift users are switching now (sunset, breach, and cost)


The decision is no longer whether to leave Drift. It is what to move to, and how fast.


### The March 2026 sunset and the 1mind migration path


On March 5, 2026,[Clari + Salesloft announced a partnership with 1mind](https://www.salesloft.com/company/newsroom/1-mind-partnership) and, in the same release, "the gradual sunset of its Drift conversational marketing solution." Under an exclusive agreement, Clari + Salesloft refers existing Drift clients to 1mind as the successor. Drift.com now redirects to a Salesloft page that reads "We've transitioned from Drift to 1mind." The announcement did not publish a completion date, so check your own contract for the practical deadline.


That referral path is the path of least resistance, not automatically the best fit. 1mind is video-first and sold through an enterprise sales process. If your pipeline leans on inbound web, compare it against the full inbound motion you need before you sign, which I cover in detail below.


### The August 2025 security incident


Many companies did not wait for the sunset. According to[Google Threat Intelligence Group](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/data-theft-salesforce-instances-via-salesloft-drift) , from as early as August 8, 2025 through at least August 18, 2025, a threat actor tracked as UNC6395 targeted Salesforce customer instances through compromised OAuth tokens associated with the Salesloft Drift application and exported large volumes of data from numerous corporate Salesforce instances. For security-sensitive buyers, that incident plus a product now in sunset was reason enough to move early.


### Why replacing Drift with another chatbot is not enough


Swapping one reactive chatbot for another preserves the least valuable part of Drift and leaves the dark funnel exactly where it was. The replacement should close the information gap: identify the visitor where that is lawful and useful, actually answer their questions from real product content, qualify, route, and follow up, not just render website chat. Drift refugees want more capability at a saner price, not a like-for-like chat clone.


## Drift chatbot alternatives: replacing the chat widget itself


A lot of searches for a "Drift chatbot alternative," "Drift chat alternatives," or an "alternative to Drift chat" come from teams that only used Drift's website chat and playbooks, not the wider Salesloft stack. If that is you, the replacement decision is simpler, and it splits three ways:


- **Like-for-like live chat with light automation:** Tidio or Intercom. Cheap to start, quick to deploy, but support-first by design.
- **AI chat that qualifies and books:** RepX, Qualified, Spara, Docket, or Warmly's Inbound Chat tier. These replace Drift playbooks with an AI agent that reasons about what the visitor asked instead of walking a decision tree.
- **Chat plus meeting routing:** if your Drift setup was mainly a front door to a calendar, Chili Piper's Experiences tier adds AI-powered chat on top of its routing and scheduling. Our roundup of[Chili Piper Chat alternatives](https://www.storylane.io/blog/chili-piper-chat-alternatives) covers that corner of the market.


The trap is choosing a chat widget because it looks closest to Drift. Scripted decision trees were the part of Drift that needed constant maintenance. If you are rebuilding anyway, rebuild on an agent that answers from your real content, which is the argument in our guide to[replacing your chatbot with an AI sales agent](https://www.storylane.io/blog/replacing-chatbot-with-ai-sales-agent) .


## How to evaluate a Drift alternative (decision criteria for inbound teams)


Before I look at any tool, I score it against what actually moves pipeline. Chat polish is not a criterion; answering buyers and converting them is. Treat time-to-value as a hard filter too: ask every vendor for a realistic go-live date on your site, in writing.


### Answer rate: the metric no one tracks


Companies track traffic, engagement, and conversion. Almost none track answer rate, the percentage of buyer questions that actually get answered before the visitor leaves. That is the number the dark funnel hides, and it is the one that predicts pipeline. An alternative that only improves chat aesthetics does not move it. An alternative that answers real product questions from grounded content, and logs what was asked, does. Ask every vendor a blunt question: can you show me what buyers asked and whether they got a correct answer.


### Chatbot vs AI sales agent


The first fork is whether the "AI" is a decision tree in disguise. Scripted bots break on edge cases and demand constant playbook maintenance. Generic AI chatbots trained on marketing copy fail a different way: they sound confident while staying vague, because marketing copy is written to impress, not to inform.


An AI sales agent is different in kind. Trained on your actual product docs, demos, and call material, it handles objections, competitor comparisons, and pricing questions with grounded, specific answers, with no rule for each path. For a fuller breakdown, see our guide to[what an AI agent for sales actually does](https://www.storylane.io/blog/ai-agent-for-sales) .


### Visitor identification and intent detection


A session-based chatbot only sees a visitor after they start typing. Several alternatives identify the company before engagement and use intent signals to separate high-fit traffic from noise. That lets you prioritize speed-to-lead where it matters and ignore the rest. If you want to learn more about identifying in-market leads, check out our guide to[buyer intent software](https://www.storylane.io/blog/buyer-intent-software) .


### Multi-channel and CRM-native follow-up


Evaluate whether the tool follows up beyond the website (email, LinkedIn, messaging apps) and how deep the CRM story goes: direct integration, automatic enrichment, and conversation summaries written to the record. Handoff-based CRM sync is not the same as deep synchronization. If summaries and qualified leads do not land in your CRM automatically, your reps re-do the work.


### Pipeline impact over chat features


My takeaway after all of this is blunt: most Drift competitors improve chat, while the best Drift alternatives improve conversion by actually answering buyers. Score on answer rate, conversion speed, lead quality, and deal velocity. Navigation help is a nice-to-have. Turning a chat into a booked meeting is the must-have.


## RepX: an AI sales agent trained on your docs and interactive demos


Full disclosure:[RepX](https://www.storylane.io/repx) is our product at Storylane, so I have skin in the game. I put it first because it is built for the dark-funnel problem, and I will be just as honest about where it stops. It is not a chat widget that routes buyers to a form; it is an AI agent you feed with your docs, website, decks, call scripts, and interactive demos, so it answers real questions with real product truth. Buyers can type, talk, or (on Premium) talk face to face with a video avatar. It qualifies against your ICP, handles objections, books meetings, and sends qualified leads plus conversation summaries to HubSpot, Salesforce, and Slack.


The angle that matters most to me: RepX proactively pulls up the relevant interactive demo inside the conversation and walks the buyer through the real product. That closes the gap between "sounds like an answer" and "is actually an answer." It is not unique in showing product (Spara lists AI demos on its Growth plan and Docket has a guided-tour feature), but it is built by a company whose core product is interactive demos, so the demo library you already have becomes the agent's best asset.


Playbooks let you set a different qualification flow per page, so your pricing page and paid landing pages each get their own questions and nudges. You can track engagements, qualified conversations, and booked meetings, and use Ask RepX to analyze what visitors asked. That is answer rate, made visible. For more on how demos turn website traffic into pipeline, see our guide to[embedding a product demo on your website to get more leads](https://www.storylane.io/blog/embed-a-product-demo-on-your-website-to-get-more-leads) .


Pricing is published: Growth starts at $2,000/month for up to 20,000 monthly visitors, Premium at $3,000/month for up to 60,000 visitors and adds the AI video avatar and visitor de-anonymization, and there is a 30-day free trial, per[storylane.io/plans](https://www.storylane.io/plans) .


The boundary, honestly: RepX is an inbound website rep, not an outbound engine. It does not build TAM lists or run cold sequences. If you need that, our[AI BDR guide](https://www.storylane.io/blog/ai-bdr) covers how to pair an outbound tool alongside an inbound agent. And if your plan only covers 20,000 visitors a month and your site gets far more, you are on Premium or Enterprise, so price that in.


## Qualified: the Salesforce-centric enterprise AI SDR


Qualified is the default enterprise choice for Salesforce-based B2B teams focused on pipeline and account-based marketing. Its AI SDR, Piper, meets buyers in real time on the website over video, voice, or live chat, follows up with inbound leads by email, books meetings, and serves personalized offers, per[qualified.com](https://www.qualified.com/piper) . Qualified says Piper has been hired by over 500 companies and lists 1,800+ five-star reviews.


The ownership changed in 2026: Salesforce[announced a definitive agreement to acquire Qualified](https://www.salesforce.com/news/press-releases/2025/12/16/salesforce-signs-definitive-agreement-to-acquire-qualified/) in December 2025, with an editor's note confirming the deal completed on April 1, 2026, and plans to bring Qualified's technology into Agentforce. Every plan on Qualified's pricing page is built around Salesforce, and it also lists HubSpot, Marketo, and other GTM integrations. Prices are not published; all tiers are quote-based.


If your revenue motion runs on Salesforce and ABM, Qualified is built for you. If you are HubSpot-first, confirm in the demo exactly what works without Salesforce at the center. For a direct head-to-head, see our[Drift vs Qualified vs Storylane RepX comparison](https://www.storylane.io/blog/drift-vs-qualified) , and for the wider field, our[Qualified alternatives](https://www.storylane.io/blog/qualified-alternatives) guide.


## Docket: inbound agent grounded in a sales knowledge lake


[Docket](https://www.docket.io/) 's strength is turning demand gen traffic into qualified pipeline the moment it lands. Its agent engages website visitors through voice or text with an on-page avatar, grounds answers in what Docket calls a Sales Knowledge Lake (product docs, CRM records, call recordings and more), and remembers visitor context across repeat visits. When it books a meeting, it syncs the conversation, qualification answers, and next steps into Salesforce or HubSpot. Docket also offers Showroom, a live guided tour of your product.


Pricing is published: Growth is $3,000/month billed annually for up to 20,000 monthly visitors, and Scale is $4,000/month for up to 100,000 visitors, adding the video avatar and multiple agents, per[docket.io/pricing](https://www.docket.io/pricing) . Standard onboarding is quoted at 7 to 14 days.


Best for: teams replacing Drift's chat widget who need qualification grounded in real buyer and account context and run active campaigns that drive the traffic. Our[Docket alternatives](https://www.storylane.io/blog/docket-alternatives) guide compares it with the rest of this tier.


## Warmly: visitor de-anonymization plus AI chat


Warmly's strength is revealing who is on your site before they engage. It describes its AI as de-anonymizing website visitors at the person level, and pairs that with an Inbound Agent for on-site conversations and a TAM Agent that runs coordinated email and ads off-site. Drift only saw visitors once they started chatting; Warmly tries to see them first.


Warmly publishes annual pricing: AI Web-Deanonymization is $10,000/year, Inbound Chat (which adds the AI chatbot and live chat) is $20,000/year, and AI Inbound Autopilot is $30,000/year, per warmly.ai/pricing.


The honest trade-off: identifying an anonymous visitor is worth little if you cannot then answer and qualify them in conversation, and the AI chat sits on the higher tiers. De-anonymization is the top of the funnel; answering and qualifying is where the pipeline is made. For a direct head-to-head, see our[Drift vs Warmly vs Storylane RepX comparison](https://www.storylane.io/blog/drift-vs-warmly) and our full list of[Warmly alternatives](https://www.storylane.io/blog/warmly-alternatives) .


## Intercom (Fin): best when support and sales overlap


Intercom's Fin AI Agent fits when deflection matters more than demo-led sales qualification. It is support-first by design. Fin's own site says it averages a 76% resolution rate across 12,000+ customers, which is impressive for support volume.


Intercom's Essential plan starts at $29/seat/month (annual), Advanced is $85 and Expert is $132 per seat/month, and Fin costs $0.99 per outcome, per intercom.com/pricing. The per-outcome model can be efficient for support and unpredictable for sales qualification on a busy marketing site. If your primary job is qualifying inbound sales conversations rather than resolving tickets, Fin is the wrong center of gravity.


## Spara, 1mind, and Knock AI: the AI-SDR challengers


These three map to distinct angles: Spara for multi-channel inbound SDR, 1mind as Salesloft's referred successor, and Knock AI for messaging-app-first teams.


### Spara: AI inbound SDR for website qualification


Spara qualifies website visitors in real time through conversational AI and works across chat, email, voice, and text. Its Starter plan is $2,100/month billed annually (chat, email, workflows), and Growth is $3,750/month, adding voice, AI demos, visitor de-anonymization, and A/B testing, per spara.com/pricing.


Is Spara better than Drift for converting inbound? For a team starting fresh in 2026, the comparison is really Spara against the other live alternatives, since Drift is in sunset. Spara is a credible pick if you want one agent across chat, email, and voice; budget for Growth if voice or demos matter. For a direct three-way comparison, see our[Drift vs Spara vs Storylane RepX breakdown](https://www.storylane.io/blog/drift-vs-spara) .


### 1mind: video-first AI avatar (Salesloft's referred successor)


1mind sells photorealistic AI "Superhumans" that qualify leads, answer product questions, deliver demos, and handle objections on the website, inside the product, and as a participant on live sales calls, per 1mind.com. It does not publish pricing. Because Clari + Salesloft refers Drift clients to 1mind, it is the default migration path for existing customers. Our[Drift vs 1mind vs Storylane RepX decision guide](https://www.storylane.io/blog/drift-vs-1mind) walks through exactly where each tool fits.


### Knock AI: multi-channel, messaging-app-first AI SDR


Knock AI lets buyers chat with you on Slack, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, and the website without creating accounts or filling out forms, and syncs enriched data to your CRM through a native integration. Pipeline Foundation starts at $1,000 to $2,000/month (Slack messaging) and Pipeline Acceleration at $1,500 to $3,500/month, which adds LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram, and iMessage, per knock-ai.com/pricing. See our[Drift vs Knock AI comparison](https://www.storylane.io/blog/drift-vs-knockai) for the detail.


Also worth considering is Chili Piper, whose Experiences tier adds AI-powered chat on top of routing and scheduling, which makes it a natural adjacent option for inbound teams weighing Drift replacements. See our[Chili Piper vs Drift comparison](https://www.storylane.io/blog/chili-piper-vs-drift) . For a broader look at the AI SDR landscape, our roundup of the[best AI SDR tools in 2026](https://www.storylane.io/blog/top-ai-sdr-tools) covers the full category.


## Is 1mind the best Drift alternative? Why the referred path is not automatically the right one


Clari + Salesloft named 1mind as Drift's successor, so it is the path of least resistance. I want to be direct about why least resistance is not the same as best fit. A vendor referral optimizes for a smooth handover inside a partner ecosystem. It does not necessarily optimize for how your B2B buyers evaluate. On three counts that decide inbound pipeline, test it hard.


### Video-first answers on the vendor's schedule, not the buyer's


1mind leads with a video avatar. Buyers who are evaluating often want to control the pace, skip to the part that applies to them, and reach their own answer. That is the finding behind our comparison of[interactive demos versus product videos](https://www.storylane.io/blog/interactive-demos-vs-product-videos) : buyers evaluate by doing, not by watching a reel. An interactive demo surfaced inside the conversation answers the question the buyer actually asked.


### The evaluation happens when no rep is around


We analyzed 1,429 off-hours buyer messages across 378 weekend conversations in our[Weekend Buyer research](https://www.storylane.io/blog/weekend-buyer-findings) . Of those 1,429 messages, 3 (about 0.2%) asked to talk to a person or to sales. Weekend buyers want to get far on their own first. So whichever tool you pick, ask how it re-engages a visitor who goes quiet or comes back to a high-intent page, and whether follow-up runs automatically by email or other channels.


### The buying committee is anonymous


Across the[637 B2B deals we studied](https://www.storylane.io/blog/what-637-b2b-deals-taught-us-about-buying-committees) , 4 in 5 buyers never joined a call. The committee does its homework unnamed. Ask every vendor, 1mind included, what it can identify before a form fill and how it routes those accounts.


None of this makes 1mind a bad product. But "referred by the vendor that is sunsetting Drift" is not, on its own, a reason to buy. If your pipeline depends on answering buyers on their own schedule, putting the right interactive demo in front of them, and re-engaging the ones who never raise their hand, compare it side by side with RepX and the others above.


## Budget and small-team options (Tidio and free tiers)


If you want Drift-style chat without an enterprise contract, budget tools exist, with real limits. Be clear-eyed about what you give up.


### Tidio with Lyro AI for small teams


Tidio offers a free plan with live chat, Lyro AI for autonomous handling of routine questions (an add-on from $32.50/month for 50 conversations), and a no-code Flows builder. It suits small businesses and early-stage startups.


### Free and low-cost entry points


Tidio's Free plan is $0 with 50 billable conversations; Starter is $24.17/month with 100 billable conversations; Growth starts from $49.17/month, per tidio.com/pricing. Free alternatives generally cover only part of the Drift motion, such as website chat, basic lead capture, or support, not conversational sales and qualification.


### Where budget tools fall short for B2B qualification


The gap for Drift-style B2B use is account-based targeting, sales-engagement integrations, and visitor identification. For an ecommerce or early-stage team, that is an acceptable trade. For an ABM motion that depends on identifying and routing target accounts, it is not enough.


## What does Drift cost, and what do Drift alternatives cost?


With the sunset announced, Drift is no longer a product to price for a new contract, and Salesloft's Drift page now points visitors to 1mind rather than to a price list. The useful comparison is between the alternatives, and here several now publish numbers: RepX from $2,000/month, Spara from $2,100/month, Docket from $3,000/month, Knock AI from $1,000/month, Warmly from $10,000/year for de-anonymization and $20,000/year for Inbound Chat, Intercom from $29/seat/month plus $0.99 per Fin outcome, and Tidio free to start. Qualified and 1mind are quote-based.


Migration costs are more than software fees. Budget for implementation, RevOps time to rebuild routing, and the risk of lost leads during the cutover. Weigh those against the replacement's subscription, not just the sticker price.


## Planning your migration off Drift without dropping pipeline


The migration is doable without disrupting inbound, but only with a plan. We have documented the full sequence in[our complete Drift migration playbook](https://www.storylane.io/blog/drift-migration) ; what follows is the condensed version. The failure mode is deactivating Drift before the replacement is capturing traffic.


### A phased cutover plan


Run it in sequence so nothing falls through:


1. Test conversation flows and routing accuracy.
2. Resolve edge cases before launch.
3. Launch the replacement in production.
4. Monitor inbound traffic, qualified-lead capture, and answer rate.
5. Deactivate Drift only after the replacement is capturing traffic successfully.


### Protecting inbound leads during the transition


To protect pipeline, prioritize a replacement that answers visitors' questions from real product content, routes on intent and fit, supports qualification playbooks, and follows up automatically. Keep both systems live briefly rather than trusting a hard cutover on day one. And make sure your demo request page is ready for the traffic: our guide on how to[boost demo signups](https://www.storylane.io/blog/demo-requests) covers it.


## The bottom line on Drift alternatives


The Drift sunset forces a decision, so make it on conversion and answer quality, not chat features. My pick for inbound teams is RepX: an AI agent trained on your own docs, decks, and interactive demos that answers buyers from real product content, shows those demos inside the conversation, syncs to HubSpot and Salesforce, and lets you measure what buyers actually asked. The rest are situational. Qualified fits a Salesforce-centric ABM motion, Spara and Docket are strong multi-channel or campaign-led agents, Warmly fits if de-anonymization is the gap, 1mind is the referred path for existing Drift customers, Knock AI suits messaging-app-first teams, and Tidio fits a budget team.


If you want to close the dark funnel rather than reskin it,[book a RepX demo](https://www.storylane.io/request-demo) and test it on your own content.


## FAQ: Drift alternatives in 2026


### Is Drift shutting down?


Drift is being gradually sunset. On March 5, 2026, Clari + Salesloft announced "the gradual sunset of its Drift conversational marketing solution" and an exclusive agreement to refer existing Drift clients to 1mind as the successor. The announcement did not give a final end date, so check your own contract terms.


### What is the best Drift alternative?


It depends on the job. For inbound qualification that answers from your own content and shows interactive demos in the conversation, RepX. For a Salesforce-centric enterprise ABM motion, Qualified. For a multi-channel AI SDR, Spara or Docket. For visitor de-anonymization first, Warmly. For a budget live chat, Tidio.


### What is the best Drift chatbot alternative for a small team?


If you only need website chat and light automation, Tidio has a free plan and paid plans from $24.17/month, and Intercom starts at $29/seat/month plus $0.99 per Fin outcome. If you want the bot to qualify and book meetings, look at the AI agents above, which start around $1,000 to $2,100/month.


### What is the best Drift alternative for HubSpot users?


RepX syncs qualified leads and conversation summaries to HubSpot (and Salesforce), Docket syncs to Salesforce or HubSpot, and Warmly and Spara also offer CRM sync. Qualified lists a HubSpot integration but its plans are built around Salesforce, so confirm the HubSpot workflow in a demo.


### Can I migrate from Drift without losing leads?


Yes, if you run a phased cutover. Test the replacement in parallel, validate routing accuracy, and only deactivate Drift once the new tool is capturing traffic successfully.


### How much do Drift alternatives cost?


Published entry prices as of October 2026: RepX from $2,000/month, Spara from $2,100/month, Docket from $3,000/month, Knock AI from $1,000/month, Warmly from $10,000/year, Intercom from $29/seat/month plus $0.99 per Fin outcome, and Tidio free. Qualified and 1mind are quote-based.
